sources.title: Supplementary material 1 Raw unprocessed videos demonstrating astrocyte GCaMP6f fluorescence in slices from tdTomato (video 1) and hPMCA2w/b animals (video 2). Frame numbers are indicated in the upper left. Original videos were acquired at 25 Hz but are presented at 125 Hz for illustration. Arrows in the hPMCA2w/b video 2 highlight two astrocytes with brief periods of activity (e.g., left arrow: frames 950–970; right arrow: frames 1042–1087). Raw unprocessed videos demonstrating neuronal GCaMP6f fluorescence in slices from tdTomato and hPMCA2w/b animals are in videos 3-7. aCSF_M4 video 3 corresponds to the field of view in  Figure 4B . aCSF_M5 video 4 corresponds to the field of view in  Figure 5B ; cocaine_M5 video 5 is the same field of view after bath application of cocaine, corresponding to  Figure 5C . aCSF_M4 video 6 is the field of view in  Figure 6B ; NPS_F9 video 7 is the same field of view after bath application of NPS-2143, corresponding to  Figure 6C . Note that the onset of neuronal fluorescence is near instantaneous rather than spreading through the soma and syncytium territories as Ca 2+  “waves” characteristic of astrocyte signals. In cases where neuronal processes are captured in the imaging plane, fluorescence in neuronal processes always accompanies fluorescence in the soma they are connected to. This is not the case for astrocyte Ca 2+  where soma and process fluorescence can be independent of each other.

sources.title: CB1R activation induces rapid remodeling of the somatodendritic region in cultured hippocampal neurons.
sources.legend: Somatodendritic region of a cultured hippocampal neuron co-expressing CB1R-eCFP, LifeAct-mCherry, and EB3-eGFP at DIV8. The axon, whose initial segment is typically strongly labeled with EB3-GFP, exits the frame in the upper-left corner. The F-actin-rich growth cone, such as shown in Video 1, is at the growing end of the axon, typically hundreds of microns away from the soma at DIV8. Treatment with 100 WIN at 10 min induces retraction of distal dendrites and broadening of proximal dendrites. Scale bar: 20 μm.
